title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 9: PCGG v. Desierto — Ombudsman Powers
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 9: CJP's account of PCGG v. Desierto (which he penned), on the investigatory and prosecutory powers of the Ombudsman and the Court's duty to reverse grave abuse
sub_topics: The Ombudsman's wide latitude of investigatory and prosecutory powers (RA 6770)
That power is not absolute — grave abuse of discretion invites reversal
PCGG v. Desierto and Disini — a dismissal reversed
The Court's constitutional duty to check the Ombudsman
signature_phrases: a wide latitude of investigatory and prosecutory prerogatives
gravely abused through a gross misappreciation of evidence

stances.claim: The Ombudsman's broad prosecutorial discretion is not absolute; when it is gravely abused, the Court has the constitutional duty to reverse it.

notable_anecdotes: CJP notes he had 'the honor of writing' the PCGG v. Desierto decision.
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 9 recounts PCGG v. Desierto and Disini — a decision CJP wrote — on the investigatory and prosecutory powers of the Ombudsman. He explains that although the Ombudsman enjoys wide latitude under RA 6770, that power is not absolute: when it is gravely abused through a gross misappreciation of evidence, the Court has the constitutional duty to reverse.
